title: Operation request
description: A request to Chaperone to perform one high-impact operation. op_hash is SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 (JCS) form of the object {spec_version, project, op, target, params}, written 'sha256:<hex>'. Chaperone recomputes it on receipt and rejects a mismatch. Every approval binds to op_hash, so an approval for one action can never authorise another. params are specific to each op kind (schemas live with the kind's adapter in Chaperone) and are opaque to this schema.

requester.description: Who asks. A run (authenticated by its run token) or the orchestrator acting in its own session. The 'run' form carries the claims Chaperone verified, not what the agent says.

target.description: What the operation acts on: the target adapter and a reference the adapter understands (repo and PR, deploy target and SHA, recipient list id).

params.description: Op-specific parameters, exactly as they will be executed.

reason.description: Free text from the requester, shown on the approval card. Untrusted; never used for authorization.

expires_at.description: After this instant the request is dead and can no longer be approved.

traceparent.description: Advisory W3C Trace Context of the caller's span. Outside op_hash: it changes with every attempt, so it can never be part of what an approval binds, and it is never used for authorization. For a run requester the trace-id SHOULD be the run's derived trace id (docs/spec.md section 8); a missing, malformed or foreign one is ignored and recorded as a trace.gap event.
